item.title: 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde
item.description: By Adeola Badru Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Governor of Edo State, has urged Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, to reconsider his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the country needed leaders committed to sustaining progress. Oshiomhole, who spoke in Ibadan on Saturday during President Bola Tinubu’s rally at the historic Mapo Hall, challenged Makinde to align himself with the wishes of the electorate, insisting that the governor must first reconsider his own position on Tinubu’s re-election bid. The former Edo governor, who expressed support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, described the forthcoming election as a decisive moment for Nigeria and questioned whether Makinde’s call for a reset was intended to reverse policies he said had benefited ordinary Nigerians. “This coming election is a decisive factor. We have a leader, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Oshiomhole said he had questions for Makinde over his position on Tinubu’s continuation in office, particularly regarding the administration’s student loan scheme, infrastructure development, and improved welfare for university lecturers. He asked whether Makinde’s opposition to the president’s re-election was connected to the federal government’s decision to provide financial assistance to students from poor backgrounds through the student loan scheme. “Is Seyi Makinde angry because Tinubu is giving loans to the children of poor people in our universities? Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he asked. The senator also questioned whether the governor intended to reverse the federal government’s infrastructure projects, particularly the coastal highway linking Lagos to Calabar, which he said would improve connectivity and make movement easier for Nigerians. “The President is creating massive infrastructure to connect Lagos to Calabar so that our people can move. Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he said. Oshiomhole further challenged Makinde’s position on the welfare of university lecturers, citing the University of Ibadan as an example of an institution that had previously experienced repeated disruptions to its academic calendar due to industrial action. He recalled that university lecturers had, in the past, frequently embarked on strikes, disrupting academic activities and delaying students’ graduation. “For this city has the most outstanding university in Africa, the University of Ibadan. For a long, long time, the lecturer will teach you for two days and then will go on strike for three days. Is that not true?” he said. The former governor said the Tinubu administration had deliberately prioritized the welfare of university lecturers, whom he described as critical to developing the country’s future workforce. item.title: Outrage as Defence Ministry publicises APC campaign rally
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ministry of Defence has come under criticism on social media after its official X account published details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid. In a post on Saturday, it announced that the rally was scheduled to hold at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 21, 2026, with Tinubu and key party officials expected to attend. It also disclosed that the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, had visited the venue on Friday night to assess security arrangements and other preparations ahead of the event. “Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state,” the post reads. “During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.” Defence Ministry/X Defence Ministry/X The post, which was accompanied by photographs of the minister’s inspection, was followed by criticism from several Nigerians, who questioned the use of an official government platform to publicise the activities of a political party. One of the critics, Kunle Adebajo, described the development as “political psychosis so deep it’s ridiculous even by Nigerian standards”. Another X user, N6, questioned the ministry’s apparent involvement in partisan activities, asking, “How is the Ministry of Defence handle clearly being Partisan. Have you lost it?” Similarly, a user identified as Dollarain2000 said, “Is this really the official handle of Nigeria’s Defence Ministry? Or the Security Directorate of the APC Presidential Campaign Council?” the user asked. Another critic, Emmanuel Doji, expressed concern over what he described as the blurring of boundaries between government responsibilities and involvement in partisan political activities. He wrote, “So what exactly is the meaning of this? The official Twitter handle of the Ministry of Defence is now publishing a political party’s campaign schedule and updates on preparations for its rally? Where exactly do we draw the line between government business and party politics? “A whole Ministry of Defence is now a publicity arm of the APC. Will it also publish the activities and campaign schedules of other political parties? This is completely inappropriate and should be condemned. Government institutions should not be turned into platforms for partisan political activities. This is not how things should be done.” Another user, Benjamin, wrote, “Defence handle of the nation doing this! No, no, no, no! This is preposterous! item.title: Haaland in VAR controversy as Man City held by Fulham
item.description: Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was contentiously ruled out. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails. But his team’s lethargic performances of late suggest otherwise, with tricky tests against Napoli on Tuesday and Arsenal next weekend threatening to extend their slump. – Slumping City – City needed a fast start to ease their anxiety and Erling Haaland almost delivered it when his looping header was cleared off the line. But Maresca has failed to fix the defensive problems that ailed City in their previous three games. Fulham took full advantage of City’s flaws to snatch the lead with an incisive counter in the 16th minute. Former City winger Oscar Bobb pounced on a wayward pass and accelerated down the right flank before picking out Muniz’s run into the penalty area. With City’s defence in disarray, Muniz kept his composure to curl a fine finish into the top corner. Maresca turned away in disgust and his frustration only increased when City were denied a leveller in the 26th minute. Iliman Ndiaye’s cross reached Haaland inside the six-yard box but the Norway striker’s weak volley was saved by Leno. Haaland’s momentum carried him into Leno and he kicked the ball over the line as the Fulham keeper struggled to get hold of it. But Haaland’s celebrations were curtailed by VAR’s decision to disallow the goal for a foul on Leno. Haaland squandered a golden opportunity to drag City level when he blazed wildly over from Phil Foden’s defence splitting pass. item.title: 2027: Tinubu takes swipe at Makinde, urges Oyo voters to choose APC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has told the people of Oyo State not to mind Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), and urged them to vote for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) from top to bottom. The president spoke on Saturday at the APC presidential rally in Ibadan, the Oyo state capital. Apparently referring to the governor, the president said, “There is a party out there parading themselves. Please don’t mind them and don’t listen to them. They are only interested in clearing what you have. Vote for APC from top to bottom.” Tinubu said he would not speak at length. “I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you. This is our party. It is your party. Is that clear? “You voted overwhelmingly for the APC last time. You must stay the course for the sake of progress, the prosperity of our country and the development of your children and great-grandchildren,” he said. Before addressing the rally, the president asked the gathering to observe a minute of silence for the victims of the boat accident in Bayelsa State. “Our condolences go to the people of Bayelsa State and the bereaved families. May God grant the people of Bayelsa peace and happiness and prevent a recurrence of such an incident. We will support them,” he said. Tinubu also announced an investment for Oyo State. “For your state, we have just signed an agreement with China’s Yutong to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport vehicles and establish an automobile assembly plant there. We will continue to bring industries. You will see progress and development,” he added. Speaking on behalf of the APC governors, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr Biodun Oyebanji, urged the Yoruba to turn out for the President. “We are appealing to the Yoruba people, particularly our sons and daughters, to come out and support the presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. On January 16, let us all come out and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Senator Sarafadeen Ali of the APC. When the time comes, we will also support our candidates contesting for the Senate, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly. “I appeal to the Yoruba people not to allow this opportunity to slip away. Let us stand together and ensure that our party succeeds in Nigeria,” Oyebanji said. The post 2027: Tinubu takes swipe at Makinde, urges Oyo voters to choose APC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
item.description: African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president. Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present. Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate. The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations. CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL gave him their “unanimous” backing. CAF has been consistently behind Infantino — who is seeking a fourth and final term — even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup. “Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said. “I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.” Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer. Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal. “You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects. On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. “He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said. McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc. “There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said. “There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands. “This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally.” The post Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu inaugurates UI medical hostel, promises 50,000 bed spaces in federal varsities
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has pledged to deliver additional 50,000 bed space hostels across federal tertiary institutions by the end of 2027 to tackle accommodation challenges confronting students Tinubu made the pledge on Saturday at the inauguration of Block E of the College of Medicine hostel, University of Ibadan (UI), located at Alexander Brown Hall, University College Hospital. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the hostel block was donated by the Chagoury family. The President, represented by the Minister of Education, Dr Maruf Alausa, said that the 50,000 bed space hostels would be delivered through the ₦400 billion Student Hostels Programme, implemented via the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs). He said the initiative was aimed at providing students with safe and decent accommodation to support their education. “The accommodation shortage at the College of Medicine has become a critical challenge following the 2020 directive of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) requiring clinical students of medicine and dentistry to reside within the University College Hospital (UCH) premises for accreditation purposes. “The college faced a shortfall of 490 bed spaces, representing 44.5 per cent of its accommodation requirement, leaving many students exposed to insecurity and difficulties attending essential clinical sessions,” the president said. According to him, the shortage also prevented the college from fully utilising its annual admission quota for the Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme. Tinubu said his administration was prioritising education funding and reforms through initiatives such as the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative, Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), TETFund and the Student Venture Capital Grant. He added that more than 36 universities had benefited from the Renewed Hope Energising Education Programme, with power installations ranging from 2.5 megawatts to 12 megawatts. The President also said that the government had completed 20 compressed natural gas (CNG) conversion centres and maintenance facilities in some universities, with 40 additional facilities expected by the end of 2028. Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of UI, Prof. Peter Olapegba, said the inauguration of Block E marked another milestone in efforts to provide adequate accommodation for medical students and meet accreditation requirements. Olapegba expressed appreciation to the benefactors, Ambassador Gilbert Ramez Chagoury and his brother, Ronald Chagoury, for their contribution to medical education. “The hostel, named the Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR Block, provides accommodation for 192 medical and dental students in 48 rooms, with four students per room. “The building also has four reading rooms, each measuring about 71 square metres, as well as rooms equipped with toilets, showers and kitchenettes,” Olapegba said. item.description: …forces 26 terrorists, family members to surrender The Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) have intensified offensives against terrorist networks, killing 21 ISWAP fighters, including senior commanders, and recording the surrender of 26 fighters and their family members in the Northeast. The Director, Defence Media Operations, Maj.-Gen. Michael Onoja, disclosed this in a statement on ongoing military operations covering Nov. 13 to Nov. 19. Onoja said precision air strikes conducted between Monday and Tuesday around Monguno and Arinna in the South Lake Chad area of Borno neutralised 21 ISWAP fighters and severely injured 10 others. He said the first strike killed seven terrorists, including members of the group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network, and incapacitated a key IED expert. According to him, the second engagement at Arinna neutralised a member of ISWAP’s Shura Council, who served as its Provost Commander, a Qaid of Sabon Tumbu and 12 other fighters. The director said the sustained military pressure also prompted 26 terrorists and their family members, comprising eight fighters and 18 family members, to surrender between Nov. 13 and Nov. 18. He said the surrender took place in Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Kukawa and Monguno Local Government Areas of Borno. Among those who surrendered were 12 women and children who fled Bula Daloye on Nov. 13, as well as a terrorist who surrendered along Gwoza-Pulka Road on Nov. 14. “The latter reportedly handed over an AK-47 rifle, five magazines, 34 rounds of ammunition and two hand grenades,” he said. Onoja said the surrendering terrorists cited intense military operations and internal clashes between rival factions as reasons for abandoning the group. He added that troops also rescued four internally displaced persons who escaped from terrorist captivity at Zaha Village in the Mandara Mountains, Gwoza LGA, on Tuesday. Onoja further disclosed that troops arrested suspected terrorist collaborators and logistics suppliers in Borno, Yobe and Kano, including individuals allegedly conveying combat materials and supplies to terrorist enclaves. In the Northwest, he said the troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued three kidnapped victims along Anka-Gada Mayya Road in Zamfara on Nov. 12 and captured a vehicle belonging to the terrorists. According to him, troops also neutralised one terrorist during an engagement at Aguba Village in Kajuru LGA of Kaduna on Nov. 14, recovering two fabricated rifles and a mobile phone. item.title: NAFDAC Destroys ₦100bn Worth Of Fake Drugs, Banned Products In Ogun
item.description: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has destroyed fake, banned, expired, substandard and falsified products worth an estimated ₦100 billion in Ogun State. The destruction exercise was carried out on Friday, 20 November 2026, at Ogwama Dumpsite, Ogere Remo, as part of the agency’s efforts to prevent unsafe and unregistered products from re-entering circulation. Speaking at the flag-off of the exercise, NAFDAC’s Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye, said the products included banned and unregistered medicines, alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles below 200ml, banned Analgin injections, expired Codeine cough syrups, Oxytocin injections, counterfeit cosmetics and unwholesome food products. She said the destruction was necessary to eliminate the risk of the products finding their way back into the Nigerian market. “As the lead agency and chair of the Federal Task Force on Fake and Counterfeit Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods, NAFDAC is resolutely committed to ensuring that food, drugs, cosmetics, medical devices, chemicals, packaged water and drinks are safe, wholesome and effective for human consumption,” she said. NAFDAC’s Director-General, Mojisola Adeyeye. Adeyeye explained that the products were recovered during enforcement operations across the country. They also included items voluntarily surrendered by compliant companies and pharmaceutical products handed over to the agency by the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS). She disclosed that NAFDAC operatives recently uncovered illegally manufactured cosmetics and unregistered pharmaceutical products in a warehouse in Lagos. According to her, the facility, which was meant for tools and hardware, had a penthouse where cosmetic products were being manufactured. Officers also recovered several cartons of Augmentin and Ampicillin packets, leaflets and other unregistered cosmetics. The agency also uncovered a facility where counterfeit versions of popular alcoholic beverage brands were being produced, while expired energy drinks were allegedly being revalidated and stored for distribution. Adeyeye said the suspects arrested during the operations would face the full wrath of the law. She added that NAFDAC officers, working with relevant authorities, had coordinated the removal of more than 100,000 cartons of banned alcoholic beverages in sachets and PET bottles from manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers in Lagos and Ogun states. The Director-General further disclosed that officers uncovered a residential building being used to manufacture and sell large quantities of unauthorised and unregistered herbal mixtures. Adeyeye commended the Nigeria Customs Service for its collaboration, particularly the handover of pharmaceutical products, including cartons of Codeine-containing cough syrups, which were among the items destroyed. item.title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list
item.description: Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement. Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special forces raid Friday night in Sinaloa state, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X. A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported. “Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said. He was captured alongside his number two in the group and another man identified as a financial operator. They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said. Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. Giving his name as Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, the FBI bulletin says his group is responsible for importing “large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States.” The post Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG increases medical student admission to 12,000, targets 20,000 annually — Alausa
item.description: The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said. Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI), on Saturday, said that it targets enrollment of 20,000 students annually. The minister said the increase in enrollment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad. He said that the government, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, had increased nursing enrollment from about 28,000 annually to more than 130,000. According to him, the country is making progress in producing more healthcare professionals. Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students. According to him, annual admission into medical schools has risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023. “We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually. “Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said. Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and other allied health programs to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce. He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrollment and improve the learning environment. The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative. “This includes the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools, and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said. Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500 billion in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds. He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical student enrollment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. (NAN) The post FG increases medical student admission to 12,000, targets 20,000 annually — Alausa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
item.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. item.title: NLC denies November 30 Jigawa strike over transport allowance
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, Jigawa State Council, has dismissed reports suggesting that it plans to embark on a strike on November 30, over the alleged failure of the state government to pay workers a N70,000 transport allowance. ‎ ‎In a statement by the State Council’s Secretary, Jide Tanko, the NLC said it was currently in discussions with the Jigawa State Government towards the prompt implementation of the N70,000 transport allowance for workers across the state for an initial six-month period. ‎ ‎The Council described the message circulating on social media as false, urging workers and members of the public to disregard it. ‎ ‎Tanko assured workers that the Council remained committed to ensuring the realisation of the allowance, adding that updates on the negotiations would be communicated through its recognised official channels. ‎ ‎He also cautioned workers against spreading unverified information, emphasising that only communications issued by the recognised NLC leadership and its affiliated unions should be regarded as authentic. ‎ ‎The Jigawa NLC Council thanked workers for their patience, understanding and continued support as engagements with the state government continue. item.title: Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president
item.description: Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election. The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja. Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Dikko said Nigeria would back Infantino’s re-election and called on other African football associations to support his continued leadership. “I must make it clear here on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all the members of CAF that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election. “This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. “We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership. “This is in our collective interest,” he added. The NSC chairman also praised Infantino’s administration, drawing on his experience in football management to argue that the FIFA president’s decisions had served the interests of the sport. “Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, and founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” he said. He maintained that Infantino’s central responsibility was to grow the game and generate more revenue, arguing that disagreements within football administration largely concerned how the funds were shared. “His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” Dikko said. Nigeria’s declaration came at the same gathering where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reiterated the continental body’s backing for Infantino’s re-election. Infantino, who became FIFA president in 2016, is seeking another four-year term at the election scheduled to hold in Morocco in March 2027 with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima set to challenge him. item.title: ‎NAS takes tiabetes screening to Abuja community‎
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA –The National Association of Seadogs (NAS) has taken diabetes awareness and free medical screening to Dutse Alhaji in Bwari Area Council, Abuja, reaching about 150 residents in a community described as underserved. ‎ ‎The outreach, organised by Zuma Deck, Galleon Bay Deck and Hopatcong Deck to mark World Diabetes Day, combined community sensitisation with diabetes and blood-pressure testing, referrals, and education on early detection and management of high or low blood sugar. ‎ ‎The delegation began with a visit to the palace of the community’s paramount leader, HRH Alhaji Abubarkar Bako. ‎ ‎Leading the medical team, Dr. Patrick Uju of NAS said the observance was established to draw attention to diabetes and the need for timely intervention. ‎ ‎“World Diabetes Day was first observed by the United Nations in 2007 to raise awareness about prevention, early diagnosis, access to treatment and the need for governments to act on diabetes,” Uju said. ‎ ‎The United Nations designated 14 November as World Diabetes Day in 2007, calling on member states and partners to promote awareness, prevention, treatment and care. ‎ ‎Mr. MacDonald Ekemezie, Second Mate of Galleon Bay Deck, said the collaboration among the three decks was deliberate. ‎ ‎“The event was organised by two onshore decks and one offshore deck of the National Association of Seadogs, and the partnership was for more coverage and more impact on the beneficiaries of the project,” Ekemezie said. ‎ ‎Hassan Mohammed, First Mate of Zuma Deck, said NAS remained committed to medical interventions in communities with limited access to healthcare. ‎ ‎“We are a non-profit advocacy and humanitarian organisation, and we intervene through medical outreaches and medical missions in underserved communities,” Mohammed said. ‎ ‎Responding to questions on funding, he said the association’s projects depend on its members. ‎ ‎“All over the world where our decks do community projects, whether humanitarian or advocacy, it relies on the contribution and generosity of its members,” Mohammed said. ‎ ‎The outreach provided screening for about 150 villagers and referrals for those who required further medical attention. item.title: ‘A fine gift to our generation’, Olajengbesi hails Davido on birthday
item.description: Human rights lawyer, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has described Afrobeats star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, as one of the fine gifts to the present generation. In a Facebook post on Saturday to celebrate the singer’s birthday, Olajengbesi, who was the campaign spokesman for the re-election of Davido’s uncle, Governor Ademola Adeleke of Osun State, applauded the greatness of the Adeleke family. Olajengbesi said, “Happy Birthday Davido, thank you for who you are to everyone who meets you. You are one of the finest gifts to our generation. I am not just grateful to you and your family, I am indebted for life. “I have seen men, I have seen great families, but I have not seen many like the Adelekes. Blessed by God, graced by men, strengthened by love, bound together by service, and united by a generosity of spirit that transcends generations. “There is something extraordinary about a family whose greatness is measured not merely by wealth, influence or accomplishments, but by the number of lives they have touched, the doors they have opened and the hope they continue to inspire in others. “I pray that the Almighty God continues to preserve you, enlarge your coast, strengthen your home and grant you greater accomplishments. May your light never grow dim, and may generations yet unborn find inspiration in the legacy you are building.” Back in September, Davido endorsed the ambition of Olajengbesi to contest the Oriade-Obokun Federal Constituency seat in the 2027 general elections. Davido had described Olajengbesi as his next project following the governor’s victory at the poll. Olajengbesi is contesting against Wole Oke of the All Progressives Congress, who has occupied the seat for 24 years. The lawyer has garnered support from the likes of popular singer Dapo Oyebanjo, aka D’banj; Spotlite Nation boss Moses Bliss; and Yoruba Nation campaigner Sunday Igboho, among others. item.title: Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil
item.description: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage. Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people. “It’s something never seen before, a movie scene,” Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media. “Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished,” he said. The hospital’s roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred. The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3 am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said. Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located. Another 32 municipalities also reported damage. This handout picture released by Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defence Department shows the damage caused by strong winds in Tupancireta, Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, on November 20, 2026. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm. “We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing,” Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defense, told Radio Gaucha. Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114 kilometers per hour (70 miles per hour) during the storm. Civil defense described the storm as a “supercell,” which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the possibility that a tornado hit the city. State officials have allocated about $330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster. Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornadoes. item.title: ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle. “The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.” Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most capped player’s rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. item.title: Young Protesters Hit Streets Across Europe
item.description: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people. Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks. The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities. But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations. Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets. “If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters. Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries. Protesters dressed up as clowns jump during a youth demonstration under the motto “Stop ReArm Europe!” ‘Lost So Much Hope’ In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide. “Austerity is social violence,” read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: “Be vegan, but eat the rich.” The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported. In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service. “I simply think it’s indefensible… to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP. While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing.
